title: Subtask decomposition for parallel work (foundational)
description: The mission plan is decomposed into subtasks with explicit inputs, expected outputs, and no hidden dependencies between them. Independence is verified by checking that no subtask's inputs include another subtask's outputs. Clean decomposition is what makes parallel investigation possible at all. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
subtasks = [{'id': 't1', 'in': ['query'], 'out': ['index latency']}, {'id': 't2', 'in': ['query'], 'out': ['cache stats']}]
indep = all('t1' not in s['in'] and 't2' not in s['in'] for s in subtasks)
print('subtasks independent:', indep, '-> safe to parallelize')
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Investigation Coordinator practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Worker assignment by capability match (foundational)
description: Each subtask is assigned to the worker whose capability profile best matches the subtask's requirements, scored by overlap of required versus offered skills. Assignment also respects current worker load so no worker is buried while others idle. The matching is recomputed if a worker fails or a new one joins mid-mission. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.

title: Progress tracking with heartbeats (foundational)
description: Workers send periodic heartbeats with their subtask's completion fraction. A missed heartbeat past the timeout marks the worker suspect and then failed, which triggers reassignment. Heartbeats turn silent worker death from a mystery into a handled event. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Investigation Coordinator practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Result merging with conflict notes (foundational)
description: Completed subtask results are merged into the mission answer in dependency order. Where two workers' results conflict, both are kept with a conflict note rather than letting one silently win. The merge preserves each result's provenance so the final answer's every section traces to its worker. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.

title: Failure reassignment protocol (foundational)
description: When a worker fails, its subtask returns to the queue with its partial progress attached, and the next-best worker picks it up from the last checkpoint rather than from zero. Reassignment is bounded: a subtask that fails three workers in a row is escalated as possibly infeasible. The protocol keeps one bad worker from sinking the mission. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
fails = {'t1': 2}
subtask = 't1'
action = 'escalate as infeasible' if fails[subtask] >= 3 else 'reassign to next worker'
print(subtask, '->', action)
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Investigation Coordinator practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.
